chapter: Cafe Society and the Zodiac Suite
title: Recording for Moe Asch and Victor, and writing in her head
summary: She recorded much for Moe Asch and for Victor ('Waltz Boogie'). She composed arrangements on the subway for her trio with J. C. Heard.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: During those years that you were at Cafe Society were you recording too?

Yes, for Moe Asch. I did a lot of records for him during that period. I did a couple of sessions for Victor. That was "Waltz Boogie". That was the first time, you know, that 3/4 was ever recorded, I mean, composed into 3/4.
That was an all-girl trio too, wasn't it?
I did that later on the session, but they wanted all boogies so I gave them about 4 boogies - "Hesitation Boogie", "Waltz Boogie", and a couple more.
What kind of writing were you doing, or were you writing then?

No, I stopped writing after I left the band and the only kind of things I'd do were arrangements for myself and the only way I did them - you see, then musicians could really hear fast. On my way down the sound of the subway would bring me inspiration and I'd write an arrangement in my head before I got to the club and I'd tell J. C. Heard (he was our drummer during this period), "I'd like to do 'Limehouse Blues'. Follow me." And he did. If the musician was just great enough, anything you did they could follow. You wouldn't have to rehearse.
Did you have a bass and drums with you?
Yes, bass and drums, no band at all.
No, it was after the 40's. It was between '41 and '42.
